from(bucket: "ftdc")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_measurement"] == "ftdc")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "systemMetrics.cpu.idle_ms" or r._field == "systemMetrics.cpu.user_ms" or r._field == "systemMetrics.cpu.iowait_ms" or r._field == "systemMetrics.cpu.nice_ms" or r._field == "systemMetrics.cpu.softirq_ms" or r._field == "systemMetrics.cpu.steal_ms" or r._field == "systemMetrics.cpu.system_ms")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: last, createEmpty: false)
  |> pivot(rowKey:["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true, columns: ["systemMetrics.cpu.idle_ms", "systemMetrics.cpu.user_ms", "systemMetrics.cpu.iowait_ms", "systemMetrics.cpu.nice_ms", "systemMetrics.cpu.softirq_ms", "systemMetrics.cpu.steal_ms", "systemMetrics.cpu.system_ms"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      _time: r._time,
      idle_ms: r["systemMetrics.cpu.idle_ms"],
      user_ms: r["systemMetrics.cpu.user_ms"],
      iowait_ms: r["systemMetrics.cpu.iowait_ms"],
      nice_ms: r["systemMetrics.cpu.nice_ms"],
      softirq_ms: r["systemMetrics.cpu.softirq_ms"],
      steal_ms: r["systemMetrics.cpu.steal_ms"],
      system_ms: r["systemMetrics.cpu.system_ms"],
      total_ms: r["systemMetrics.cpu.idle_ms"] + r["systemMetrics.cpu.user_ms"] + r["systemMetrics.cpu.iowait_ms"] + r["systemMetrics.cpu.nice_ms"] + r["systemMetrics.cpu.softirq_ms"] + r["systemMetrics.cpu.steal_ms"] + r["systemMetrics.cpu.system_ms"]
  }))
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      _time: r._time,
      user: 100.0 * float(v: r.user_ms) / float(v: r.total_ms),
      system: 100.0 * float(v: r.system_ms) / float(v: r.total_ms),
      nice: 100.0 * float(v: r.nice_ms) / float(v: r.total_ms),
      idle: 100.0 * float(v: r.idle_ms) / float(v: r.total_ms),
      iowait: 100.0 * float(v: r.iowait_ms) / float(v: r.total_ms),
      softirq: 100.0 * float(v: r.softirq_ms) / float(v: r.total_ms),
      steal: 100.0 * float(v: r.steal_ms) / float(v: r.total_ms)
  }))

panels.title: Write Concern

panels.description:
Tickets Available Read displays the number of read tickets available to the WiredTiger storage engine. Read tickets represent the number of concurrent read operations allowed into the storage engine. When this value reaches zero, new read requests might queue until a read ticket becomes available.

Tickets Available Write displays the number of write tickets available to the WiredTiger storage engine. Write tickets represent the number of concurrent write operations allowed into the storage engine. When this value reaches zero, new write requests might queue until a write ticket becomes available.

panels.title: WiredTiger Cache Activity

panels.description:
Clean vs dirty data

Clean refers to data in the cache that is identical to the version stored on disk.
Dirty refers to data in the cache that has been modified and needs to be reconciled with the data stored on the disk.

Clean vs dirty eviction

In the case of clean eviction, there is no dirty content on the page and it is directly removed from the memory. After that, the page remains solely on the disk unchanged.
In the case of dirty eviction, the dirty page goes through reconciliation. The obsolete content on the page is thrown out, the latest value goes to the data store and older values go to the history store.

panels.description:
scanned: Represents the number of index keys examined during query execution in MongoDB. This metric indicates the count of index entries evaluated by the query engine while processing queries or find operations. Monitoring the number of keys examined helps you assess the efficiency of your queries and index usage. It allows you to optimize query execution, improve index selection, and reduce the overall number of index entries processed during query evaluation.

scannedObjects: Represents the number of documents examined during query execution in MongoDB. This metric indicates the count of documents evaluated by the query engine while processing queries or find operations. Monitoring the number of documents examined helps you understand the extent of document scanning and processing during query execution. It allows you to optimize query performance, improve query plans, and reduce the overall number of documents processed during query evaluation.

panels.title: Query Executor

panels.description:
Returned: Represents the number of documents returned by read operations in MongoDB. This metric indicates the count of documents retrieved as a result of queries or find operations. Monitoring the number of returned documents helps you assess the efficiency and effectiveness of your read operations, allowing you to optimize query performance and ensure accurate retrieval of the desired data.

Updated: Represents the number of documents updated by write operations in MongoDB. This metric indicates the count of documents modified as a result of update operations. Monitoring the number of updated documents helps you track the frequency of updates and assess the impact of write operations on your data. It allows you to optimize update operations, ensure data consistency, and track the effectiveness of any modifications made to your documents.

Inserted: Represents the number of documents inserted by write operations in MongoDB. This metric indicates the count of new documents added to the database as a result of insert operations. Monitoring the number of inserted documents helps you track the rate of data creation or ingestion, assess data growth patterns, and ensure the proper functioning of your data insertion processes.

Deleted: Represents the number of documents deleted by write operations in MongoDB. This metric indicates the count of documents removed from the database as a result of delete operations. Monitoring the number of deleted documents helps you track the frequency of data removal, assess data cleanup processes, and ensure the proper management of your data lifecycle.

panels.description:
This metric reflects the current state of a MongoDB replica set member, where each member’s state is represented by a numeric code defined by MongoDB.

It helps determine whether a node is PRIMARY, SECONDARY, ARBITER, DOWN, etc.

Common State Codes:

0 - STARTUP
1 - PRIMARY
2 - SECONDARY
3 - RECOVERING
5 - STARTUP2
6 - UNKNOWN
7 - ARBITER
8 - DOWN
9 - ROLLBACK
10 - REMOVED

targets.query:

  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _field: strings.replaceAll(v: strings.replaceAll(v: r._field, t: "replSetGetStatus.", u: ""), t: ".health", u: "") }))

panels.description: This metric represents the replication lag between the primary node and each secondary member in the MongoDB replica set. It measures how much time (in seconds) a replica member is behind the primary in applying the latest operations.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "ftdc")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_measurement"] == "ftdc")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_field"] =~ /replSetGetStatus\.members\.\d+\.lastAppliedWallTime|serverStatus\.localTime/)
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: last, createEmpty: false)
  |> pivot(rowKey:["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      _time: r._time,
      member_0: if exists r["replSetGetStatus.members.0.lastAppliedWallTime"] then (float(v: r["serverStatus.localTime"]) - float(v: r["replSetGetStatus.members.0.lastAppliedWallTime"])) / 1000.0 else 0.0,
      member_1: if exists r["replSetGetStatus.members.1.lastAppliedWallTime"] then (float(v: r["serverStatus.localTime"]) - float(v: r["replSetGetStatus.members.1.lastAppliedWallTime"])) / 1000.0 else 0.0,
      member_2: if exists r["replSetGetStatus.members.2.lastAppliedWallTime"] then (float(v: r["serverStatus.localTime"]) - float(v: r["replSetGetStatus.members.2.lastAppliedWallTime"])) / 1000.0 else 0.0,
      member_3: if exists r["replSetGetStatus.members.3.lastAppliedWallTime"] then (float(v: r["serverStatus.localTime"]) - float(v: r["replSetGetStatus.members.3.lastAppliedWallTime"])) / 1000.0 else 0.0,
      member_4: if exists r["replSetGetStatus.members.4.lastAppliedWallTime"] then (float(v: r["serverStatus.localTime"]) - float(v: r["replSetGetStatus.members.4.lastAppliedWallTime"])) / 1000.0 else 0.0,
      member_5: if exists r["replSetGetStatus.members.5.lastAppliedWallTime"] then (float(v: r["serverStatus.localTime"]) - float(v: r["replSetGetStatus.members.5.lastAppliedWallTime"])) / 1000.0 else 0.0,
      member_6: if exists r["replSetGetStatus.members.6.lastAppliedWallTime"] then (float(v: r["serverStatus.localTime"]) - float(v: r["replSetGetStatus.members.6.lastAppliedWallTime"])) / 1000.0 else 0.0,
      member_7: if exists r["replSetGetStatus.members.7.lastAppliedWallTime"] then (float(v: r["serverStatus.localTime"]) - float(v: r["replSetGetStatus.members.7.lastAppliedWallTime"])) / 1000.0 else 0.0,
      member_8: if exists r["replSetGetStatus.members.8.lastAppliedWallTime"] then (float(v: r["serverStatus.localTime"]) - float(v: r["replSetGetStatus.members.8.lastAppliedWallTime"])) / 1000.0 else 0.0,
      member_9: if exists r["replSetGetStatus.members.9.lastAppliedWallTime"] then (float(v: r["serverStatus.localTime"]) - float(v: r["replSetGetStatus.members.9.lastAppliedWallTime"])) / 1000.0 else 0.0,
  }))
  |> yield(name: "differences")
